setup_notes: Fork main fast-forwarded to upstream (already up to date at e64ff12f). Release CLI has no --stats flag; measurements use wall time (hyperfine/benchmark tool) and CPU profiles. Benchmark tool flagged several runs unreliable due to machine noise (4 vCPU); the first reproducer (star_100x8000) stayed unreliable after the re-run, so verification was re-done on star_300x4000, where time was reliable.

hypotheses.title: Stage 6 eagerly tabulates every public symbol of every imported module, per importing module (scope.NewPackage)
hypotheses.issue: At the start of semantic analysis (stage 6), semantics/internal/analysis/scope/context.go:NewPackage (called once per module from analysis.Analyze) iterates space.PublicMainSymbols() of EVERY imported module (explicit imports plus implicit lang-lib imports). For each public symbol it calls ctx.ValueSymbolMetadata(ref) (sync.Map load) and ctx.SymbolType(ref) (global symbolSpacesMu RLock), and inserts a VarDecl into a non-presized moduleVars map. The iteration itself (model/symbol.go:ExportedSymbolSpace.PublicMainSymbols -> SymbolSpace.Symbols/SymbolAt) takes a shared RWMutex per symbol, from every concurrently running module. The table is only read through packageContext.ModuleVar(sym) (isolation/lock rules, e.g. analysis/statements.go, analysis/declarations.go), and only for the few imported symbols a module actually references. So each module pays O(total exports of its imports) regardless of usage: O(modules x exports) for a shared 'common' module, O(M^2*P) for dense import graphs. On a 100-module package importing one module with 16000 exports, NewPackage was ~59% of all frontend CPU and ~98% of stage 6.

reproducer.generator:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Star-shaped package: one `common` module exporting E public consts+functions,
imported by M small modules that each use one symbol of it."""
import os, sys, shutil
out = sys.argv[1]; M = int(sys.argv[2]); E = int(sys.argv[3])
shutil.rmtree(out, ignore_errors=True); os.makedirs(out)
open(os.path.join(out, 'Ballerina.toml'), 'w').write('[package]\norg = "h1"\nname = "starpkg"\nversion = "0.1.0"\n')
d = os.path.join(out, 'modules', 'common'); os.makedirs(d)
o = []
for p in range(E):
    o.append(f'public const int C{p} = {p};')
    o.append(f'public function f{p}(int a) returns int {{ return a + {p}; }}')
open(os.path.join(d, 'common.bal'), 'w').write('\n'.join(o) + '\n')
for i in range(M):
    d = os.path.join(out, 'modules', f'm{i}'); os.makedirs(d)
    open(os.path.join(d, f'm{i}.bal'), 'w').write(
        f'import starpkg.common;\npublic function entry() returns int {{ return common:f{i % E}({i}); }}\n')
main = [f'import starpkg.m{i};' for i in range(M)]
main.append('public function main() {\n    int s = ' + ' + '.join(f'm{i}:entry()' for i in range(M)) + ';\n    if s < 0 { panic error("x"); }\n}')
open(os.path.join(out, 'main.bal'), 'w').write('\n'.join(main) + '\n')

hypotheses.fix_approach: Keep only the module's own global variables/constants in moduleVars eagerly. In NewPackage, record just the SpaceIndex of each imported module's main symbol spaces (a handful of entries). In packageContext.ModuleVar, on a miss, resolve the ref on demand: accept it only if its SpaceIndex is an imported main space, SymbolIsPublic(ref), and ValueSymbolMetadata(ref) is ok with !md.Parameter (same filter as the old eager loop); build the same VarDecl and memoize hits in moduleVars. Plain map writes are safe because a packageContext is per module and stage 6 analysis is sequential within a module. Imported modules' symbols/types are complete after stages 3-4, so the deferred read is equivalent. Pitfalls: preserve the miss behaviour for non-imported/non-public refs; ModuleVar unnarrows the ref first. After the fix nothing in the compiler calls PublicMainSymbols (only ls/). Remaining cost on these reproducers is GC over the large live heap and semtypes.ContextFrom per function body (unrelated). Benchmarks on this 4-vCPU machine are noisy (CV 4-8%); larger reproducers gave more stable results.

notes: Exploration also noticed (not pursued): 600 nested blocks or 500+ nested ifs panic with 'diagnostics: StartLine: failed to resolve startOffset -NNN' (crash, not perf). DiagnosticEnv.FileIndex takes an RLock per AST node (~3% of AST build); getRecMappingAtomType takes a global mutex on reads.
